title: Grammar basics
description: A short Rule 4 lesson: preferred order, particles, negation, serial verbs, questions, and the Actor always spoken. This seed stores no Fonoran: every answer is compiled from the deterministic translator at build/runtime, tips resolve {particle:…}/{concept:…}/{particles} placeholders from the seeds, and choose distractors are either a compiled contrast sentence or a mechanical token transform.

exercises.tip: Present has no time particle. Past = {particle:tense_past} · Future = {particle:tense_future}. The action word never changes.
Put {particle:tense_past} next to the action for past. Still: Actor → Action → Target.
Negation {particle:logic_not} sits immediately in front of what it denies.
Particles are tiny and closed: {particles}. Type only the grammar particles you see.

exercises.sourceText: I want to go to the water.
exercises.tip: Want + go stacks in the Action: {concept:want} {concept:move}. Do not park the second verb as the object.

exercises.sourceText: Do you want to go to the beach?
exercises.promptLang: Which means “do you want to go to the beach?”

distractor.sourceText: You want to go to the beach.

exercises.tip: Questions open with {particle:clause_question}. Without it, you have made a statement.

exercises.sourceText: Do you want to go to the beach?
exercises.promptLang: Which is correct for “do you want to go to the beach?”
exercises.tip: The Actor is always spoken. A yes/no to “you” keeps {concept:addressee} — without it, nobody is named.
Preferred order: Actor → Action → Target. Type the full roman phrase.
{particle:logic_if} joins the condition to the result. The action word keeps the same spelling in both halves.
Words never inflect and there is no “is/are” — a state word stands alone after the Actor.
